children: Axis AMC Alternates completely exited retail giant Avenue Supermarts (DMart) and state-run power financier REC Limited in its Axis Pure Contra PMS strategy during July. The fund cited margin compression from aggressive quick-commerce competition and rising state utility credit risks.

According to the fund house’s latest portfolio disclosures, the strategy redeployed capital into alternative consumer and financial bets. These include fresh entries in Paytm parent One 97 Communications (3.86%) and Jio Financial Services (5.35%). DMart was eliminated over concerns of intensifying retail format wars.

The portfolio reshuffle reflects institutional caution over brick-and-mortar hypermarkets facing disruption from 10-to-15-minute grocery delivery platforms. In its commentary, the investment team noted that DMart was sold due to rising competitive intensity across modern retail formats. This could impair the supermarket operator’s medium-term margin trajectory.
Simultaneously, the fund exited non-banking financial company REC Ltd on expectations of moderating loan growth and heightened exposure to state power distribution utility credit profiles.

Following the restructuring, the Axis Pure Contra PMS strategy holds 29 stocks. Large-caps account for 49%, small-caps make up 36.2%, and mid-caps stand at 10.6%. Financial services form the largest sectoral allocation at 32.6%. Automobile and auto components follow at 14.5%, while telecommunications stands at 7.1%.

Indus Towers emerged as the strategy's single largest holding at 7.12%. Automaker Mahindra & Mahindra followed closely at 6.90%. Other prominent bets in the top 10 include Jio Financial Services (5.35%), Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC (4.76%), ICICI Bank (4.66%), luxury retailer KDDL Ltd (4.28%), Larsen & Toubro (4.04%), Motherson Sumi Wiring India (4.04%), Hindustan Unilever (3.93%), and One 97 Communications (3.86%).

Bajaj Finance, Mahindra & Mahindra, and Jio Financial Services served as top monthly performance contributors. CIE Automotive India, Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC, and Bank of Baroda acted as key detractors. Since its inception on November 27, 2020, the Pure Contra strategy has delivered a consolidated Time-Weighted Rate of Return (TWRR) of 18.72% against 15.96% for the BSE 500 TRI.
Axis AMC's best performer: Kaizen strategy ramps up small-cap allocation, churns pharma basket

Across other listed alternate offerings, the high-conviction Axis Kaizen PMS expanded its small-cap footprint to 65.1% across a concentrated 20-stock portfolio. Mid-caps stand at 12.1% and large-caps at 10.1%. Capital goods (25.8%), healthcare (22.6%), and automobile components (22.0%) dominate the Kaizen asset mix, together representing 82.9% of the portfolio.

During July, the Kaizen strategy reshuffled its healthcare basket by adding Blue Jet Healthcare. The team cited its differentiated contrast-media product portfolio and long-term capacity expansion pipeline. Conversely, it completely dumped Cohance Lifesciences on expectations of near-term financial weakness driven by a subdued short-term drug pipeline.

Auto component supplier Sansera Engineering remains the Kaizen portfolio's largest holding at 12.99%. Acutaas Chemicals follows at 10.66%, UltraTech Cement at 7.45%, Syrma SGS Technology at 5.58%, and CIE Automotive India at 5.42%. Turnaround play Wockhardt also features in Kaizen’s top 10 holdings with a 3.95% weight.

Jubilant Ingrevia, Sansera Engineering, and UltraTech Cement drove the month's positive attribution. Acutaas Chemicals, Kirloskar Pneumatic, and CIE Automotive weighed on performance. Since its inception on June 15, 2023, the Kaizen strategy has delivered a TWRR of 23.24% compared to 13.55% for the BSE 500 TRI.

The Axis Pure Growth PMS strategy maintained a 26-stock book spanning large-caps (42.5%), small-caps (36.6%), and mid-caps (8.0%). Healthcare (17.6%), financial services (16.5%), and automobile/auto components (12.4%) represent the top three sector weights.
Axis AMC's Pure Growth Strategy PMS

The Pure Growth strategy's largest holding is luxury watch retailer KDDL Ltd at 7.14%. Maruti Suzuki India followed at 7.01%, Bharti Airtel at 6.74%, Acutaas Chemicals at 6.56%, ICICI Bank at 6.30%, UltraTech Cement at 5.69%, Ajanta Pharma at 4.56%, and Eternal Ltd (formerly Zomato Ltd) at 4.43%.

Top monthly contributors for Pure Growth were Bharti Airtel, UltraTech Cement, and Sun Pharmaceutical Industries. Acutaas Chemicals, HDFC Bank, and CIE Automotive were the top detractors. The strategy trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 30.8x against 21.9x for the BSE 500. It has delivered a since-inception return of 16.64% versus 13.79% for its benchmark.

Statutory disclosures from the factsheet indicate that the portfolios were formally transferred to Axis AMC from Axis Securities Limited effective July 6, 2026. Naveen Kulkarni, who previously led investments as Chief Investment Officer at Axis Securities, continues at the helm as Chief Investment Officer – PMS & Listed Equity Alternates at Axis AMC.

title: Axis AMC PMS fund dumps DMart on q-comm squeeze, exits REC over state discom credit risks
